note: Whisker & Brew resident preferences, room simulation and café operations are fictional educational simulation data.

residents.name: Mocha
residents.bio: Quiet by default. Mocha likes observation, high places and having an obvious way out.

residents.name: Chai
residents.bio: Chai investigates new routes first and decides about humans later.

residents.name: Latte
residents.bio: Latte prefers slow enrichment, bird-watching and predictable voices.

residents.name: Kopi
residents.bio: Kopi has opinions about every toy and will test the physics of your furniture.

residents.name: Miso
residents.bio: Miso prefers a little distance and a very good view of what everyone else is doing.

residents.name: Tofu
residents.bio: Tofu considers food puzzles a legitimate engineering discipline.

residents.name: Mochi
residents.bio: Mochi is social on her own terms and likes humans who understand consent cues.

residents.name: Echo
residents.bio: Echo notices the room before entering it. Low traffic and escape routes matter a lot.

objects.name: Quiet nook
objects.hint: A protected place to opt out.

objects.name: Window seat
objects.hint: Watch without being in the middle of things.

rooms.name: Sunroom
rooms.description: A sunny observation room with perches, windows and soft resting options.

rooms.name: Quiet Garden
rooms.description: Low stimulation, protected paths and retreat-first design.

rooms.name: Play Loft
rooms.description: Vertical routes, enrichment and short bursts of activity.

rooms.name: Café Floor
rooms.description: The busiest room. Humans can interact, but cats always keep an exit.

events.title: A visitor has started calling a hiding cat out.
choices: Ask them to give the cat space
Open the hide so the visitor can see
Offer food to lure the cat out
events.why: A retreat only works when the cat can use it without being pursued.

events.title: The room gets noticeably louder.
choices: Increase the music so they adapt
events.why: Address the environmental stressor before asking residents to tolerate more stimulation.

events.title: A resident walks away during interaction.
choices: Pick them up so they stay
events.why: Leaving is useful information. Respecting the exit preserves choice and predictability.
